svg.title: Crimping a Molex SL terminal, step by step
svg.desc: Animated, six steps in a 12 second loop, with a numbered step list that lights up in step. 1: strip 0.100-0.125 in (2.5-3.2 mm) from 22-24 AWG wire; the cut piece of insulation slides off the bare strands. 2: the terminal (Molex 16-02-0103) lies open in the jaws of the Molex 63811-8700 hand tool and the wire slides in, bare copper under the conductor crimp and insulation under the insulation crimp. 3: the jaws close and both crimps fold around the wire. 4: check the crimp, front to back: nothing in the contact; the conductor crimp on bare copper only, seam closed; the strands 0-0.04 in (0-1.0 mm) past it; a window where copper and insulation both show; the insulation crimp gripping the insulation. 5: push the terminal into the housing until it latches; pin 1, the one the triangle on the housing marks, takes CAN-H, the bus's own color and never green; pin 2 takes CAN-L, always green. 6: tug each wire, one at a time; a good 24 AWG crimp holds 6.5 lb. A still panel shows the housing's end view: the triangle marks pin 1, CAN-H there, green CAN-L on pin 2, the same on every plug. With reduced motion the drawing shows the checked crimp.
svg.text: Crimping a Molex SL terminal, step by step
Terminal 16-02-0103 for 22–24 AWG wire · Molex hand tool 63811-8700
Lay it in the Molex 63811-8700 tool.
bare copper under the conductor crimp
the crimps fold around the wire
copper only in it; nothing in the contact
Push it into the housing until it latches.
Tug each wire, one at a time.
a good 24 AWG crimp holds 6.5 lb
